Quadratic function and its graph: y = ax² + bx + c with a ≠ 0 has a parabola as its graph. The sign of a sets the direction of the branches, c is the y-intercept, and the zeros come from the discriminant D = b² − 4ac.
Properties of the parabola: The vertex is at x₀ = −b / (2a) and the axis of symmetry is x = x₀. For a > 0 the vertex gives the minimum value, for a < 0 the maximum.
Quadratic inequalities: Find the zeros, sketch the parabola, then read off where it is above or below the x-axis. Include the zeros only for ≥ and ≤.
The interval method: Factor, mark zeros on a number line (denominator zeros are excluded), check one sign, alternate signs, and pick the intervals that match the inequality.
